explanation: Once the first sperm gets inside, the egg quickly changes its outer shell (zona pellucida) into a tough shield so no other sperm can squeeze through.

question: How does asking about a patient's family medical history help during a musculoskeletal assessment?

options.A: It replaces the need to perform a physical examination of the joints
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will develop the exact same surgical complications
options.C: It shows the exact dietary habits of the patient's household
options.D: It highlights inherited conditions like gout or osteoporosis that may affect the patient

explanation: You got it! Many bone and joint problems run in families, so knowing the family history helps you spot risks early.

question: Which health problem is most common among street populations due to a lack of clean drinking water and toilets?

options.A: Waterborne diarrheal diseases
options.B: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.C: Hereditary bleeding disorders
options.D: Congenital heart defects

explanation: Spot on. Without safe drinking water and good sanitation, tummy infections and diarrhea spread very easily.

question: A female client is afraid to ask for modern contraceptives because her husband opposes them. What does this show?

options.A: A shortage of medical supplies
options.B: Poor personal hygiene habits
options.C: An allergy to birth control
options.D: Gender power imbalances

explanation: That's right! When one partner cannot make independent health choices due to spousal control, it highlights an underlying power imbalance.

question: How can a transport nurse best prepare for potential medical equipment failure during a trip?

options.A: Turn off monitors to conserve power for emergencies
options.B: Disable all battery alarms to keep the cabin quiet
options.C: Carry spare batteries and manual backup devices
options.D: Rely entirely on the vehicle's electrical system

explanation: Tech can fail us when we least expect it. Having extra batteries and manual tools like a bag-valve-mask ensures you're always ready to save the day.

question: What is the very first thing you should do right after pulling the needle out of your patient's skin?

options.A: Massage the injection site vigorously with an alcohol swab
options.B: Recap the needle carefully using both hands
options.C: Engage the safety device and drop it into a sharps container
options.D: Place the used syringe on the bedside table for later disposal

explanation: Safety first! Always pop the safety shield on and drop it straight into the sharps box to keep yourself and others safe from accidental pricks.

question: Why must community health nurses work closely with WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) teams in an IDP camp?

options.A: Clean water and proper sanitation directly prevent waterborne infectious diseases
options.B: Sanitation workers handle the psychiatric evaluation of adults
options.C: Nurses need assistance with ordering hospital furniture
options.D: WASH engineers are responsible for diagnosing clinical malaria

explanation: Good health in a camp relies heavily on clean water and toilets, making teamwork between nurses and WASH teams a must.

question: Which organization sets the foundational legal and professional practice boundaries for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: National Union of Local Government Employees
options.B: West African Health Education Board
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)
options.D: Nigerian Medical Association Financial Committee

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body responsible for regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h5)

question: During a neuro exam, a patient struggles to quickly flip their hand back and forth to tap their palm. What is this finding called?

options.A: Cerebellar nystagmus
options.B: Expressive aphasia
options.C: Dysdiadochokinesia
options.D: Peripheral neuropathy

explanation: It's a big mouthful of a word, but 'dysdiadochokinesia' just describes trouble performing fast, alternating movements smoothly. You are well on your way to acing your clinical postings!

question: A nurse wants to see if patient age relates to how often falls happen, without changing anything or giving any treatment. Which design fits best?

options.A: Correlational design
options.B: True experimental design
options.C: Clinical intervention trial
options.D: Qualitative ethnography

explanation: Great job if you picked correlational! This design simply looks at how two variables relate to each other in the real world, without the researcher interfering.

question: Why can using harsh, strong soaps every day damage the skin?

options.A: They permanently block all normal sweat gland secretions
options.B: They strip away the natural protective lipid barrier
options.C: They increase the thickness of the subcutaneous fat layer
options.D: They cause an immediate and permanent loss of skin pigment

explanation: Exactly! Harsh soaps wash away your skin's friendly natural oils, leaving it dry, angry, and irritated.

question: A patient needs an IV that won't get blocked every time they bend their arm. Which spot should you avoid?

options.A: The dorsal metacarpal network
options.B: The antecubital fossa
options.C: The back of the hand
options.D: The lower forearm veins

explanation: The antecubital fossa sits right at the inner elbow crease. When the patient bends their arm, the tubing kinks and the pump starts beeping. Better to pick a spot on the forearm or hand!

question: A mother brings in her infant who is very sleepy (lethargic) and vomiting everything she feeds her. According to IMCI, what do these signs mean?

options.A: Normal infant behavior during a mild growth spurt
options.B: Minor symptoms that can be treated at home with rest
options.C: Side effects of routine immunization that need no action
options.D: General danger signs requiring urgent hospital referral

explanation: Spot on! Lethargy and inability to keep fluids down are red-flag danger signs. They mean the baby needs emergency hospital care right away.

question: Where should you NEVER inject a local painkiller (anesthetic) that contains adrenaline?

options.A: On the tip of the nose or fingers
options.B: Across the front of the thigh
options.C: On the fleshy part of the upper back
options.D: Along a straight scalp laceration

explanation: Adrenaline makes blood vessels squeeze shut. In delicate areas like fingers and noses, this can completely cut off blood supply and damage the tissue. Good to know for clinical practice!

question: Why does a nurse listen to the chest with a stethoscope during a respiratory assessment?

options.A: To detect normal breath sounds and abnormal adventitious sounds
options.B: To measure the exact blood pressure inside the lung tissue
options.C: To feel vibrations of the vocal cords through the chest wall
options.D: To check for skin temperature differences across the ribs

explanation: Auscultation allows the nurse to hear air moving through the airways and identify sounds like wheezes or crackles that indicate disease. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which type of diarrhoea happens when inflammation causes blood, pus, and mucus to leak into the bowel?

options.A: Osmotic diarrhoea
options.B: Secretory diarrhoea
options.C: Exudative diarrhoea
options.D: Motility diarrhoea

explanation: When the gut lining gets inflamed and 'weeps' fluid, blood, or mucus—like in a bad infection or IBD—we call it exudative diarrhoea. Great nursing vocabulary to keep in your toolkit!

question: Why must all research assistants follow the exact same steps when collecting data?

options.A: To make the research study finish in a single afternoon
options.B: To eliminate the need for any written documentation
options.C: To ensure the patients finish their hospital meals faster
options.D: To prevent personal bias and reduce random measurement errors

explanation: You got it! Following a standard procedure ensures that everyone collects data the same way, keeping our results accurate and unbiased.

question: In which year did the World Health Organization publish its first model list of essential medicines?
explanation: The World Health Organization introduced the very first model list in 1977 to help countries prioritize public health needs. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why do young teens sometimes look a bit clumsy or awkward?

options.A: The brain shrinks temporarily during a growth spurt
options.B: Bones grow faster than the supporting muscles and tendons
options.C: Vision blurs due to rapid eyeball enlargement
options.D: Inner ear fluid production increases rapidly

explanation: Correct! Their bones shoot up faster than their muscles can keep up with, which temporarily throws off their balance and coordination.

question: A patient with endocarditis has small, painful reddish bumps on their finger pads. What are these called?

options.A: Petechiae
options.B: Roth spots
options.C: Osler's nodes
options.D: Janeway lesions

explanation: Osler's nodes are tender, painful bumps that pop up on fingers and toes due to immune complexes settling there. Remember: O for 'Ouch' in Osler's! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why does a lower pH number mean higher acidity?

options.A: A lower number shows that bicarbonate levels have increased
options.B: A lower number indicates fewer metabolic wastes in the plasma
options.C: A lower number represents a complete lack of dissolved gases
options.D: A lower number means a higher amount of free hydrogen ions

explanation: Think of it this way: the more free hydrogen ions pile up, the more acidic the fluid becomes, and the lower the pH number drops. You've got this!

question: Why is it smart to involve traditional birth attendants (TBAs) in community safe motherhood programs?

options.A: To train them to recognize danger signs and refer women promptly
options.B: To grant them full authority to perform major surgeries
options.C: To eliminate the need for any modern medical clinics
options.D: To replace licensed nurses in major teaching hospitals

explanation: Many rural women trust TBAs. Training TBAs to spot trouble early means they can send mums to the hospital before it's too late.

question: A patient comes to the clinic complaining of constant thirst, frequent urination, and sudden weight loss. What condition should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Chronic kidney disease
options.B: Diabetes mellitus
options.C: Urinary tract infection
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: The classic trio of excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unexplained weight loss strongly points toward new-onset diabetes mellitus. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h2)

question: You notice a fellow nurse showing signs of severe impairment while on duty. What is the best professional step to take?

options.A: Keep the secret permanently and let the impaired nurse handle critical drug doses alone
options.B: Report the observation safely through institutional channels to protect patients and help the colleague
options.C: Steal some of the leftover medications for personal use after the shift ends
options.D: Shout insults at the colleague in front of patients and visitors in the hallway

explanation: Patient safety always comes first, but we also want to guide our struggling colleagues toward the help they need through proper, confidential channels.

question: When would a nurse researcher choose a qualitative design?

options.A: To test a specific drug dosage on a group of people
options.B: To prove cause and effect using large numerical samples
options.C: To quickly measure blood pressure across a large population
options.D: To explore the emotional details of a patient's illness

explanation: Great thinking! We use qualitative designs when we want rich, descriptive stories about human experiences instead of cold numbers.

question: What is the main goal of performing a colposcopy in a clinic setting?

options.A: To surgically remove the entire uterus and surrounding lymph nodes
options.B: To collect a blood sample for complete blood count analysis
options.C: To destroy pre-cancerous lesions using extreme freezing temperatures
options.D: To magnify and closely inspect the cervix for abnormal tissue

explanation: Spot on! A colposcope is basically a special magnifying glass with a light. It helps healthcare providers get a close-up look at the surface of the cervix to check for any trouble spots.

question: Which communication style involves stating your professional concerns clearly without being aggressive or overly timid?

options.A: Silent withdrawal
options.B: Assertive communication
options.C: Aggressive confrontation
options.D: Passive communication

explanation: Correct! Assertiveness lets you stand up for your patients and your views firmly and professionally, keeping respect on all sides.

question: Which section of a report gives you the first overview of the clinical problem and study goals?

options.A: The methodology
options.B: The appendices
options.C: The reference list
options.D: The introduction

explanation: The introduction sets the stage, telling you why the study was done and what it hopes to achieve.

question: Which group of blood pressure medications must be strictly avoided during pregnancy because they can harm the baby's kidneys?

options.A: Beta-blockers
options.B: Calcium channel blockers
options.C: ACE inhibitors
options.D: Centrally acting alpha agonists

explanation: Remember: ACE inhibitors are known to mess with how a baby's kidneys develop, so doctors steer clear of them during pregnancy.

question: Why are lower respiratory infections generally more serious than upper respiratory ones?

options.A: They cause severe localized pain in the nose.
options.B: They only happen to people with heart disease.
options.C: They directly interfere with oxygen exchange in the air sacs.
options.D: They are always completely resistant to drugs.

explanation: You've got this! When an infection hits the tiny air sacs (alveoli) deep in the lungs, it blocks oxygen from getting into the blood, making it much harder to breathe.

question: Which of these is a classic example of a biological agent?

options.A: A deficiency of protein in the diet
options.B: A bacterium causing a wound infection
options.C: Lead poisoning from old water pipes
options.D: Ultraviolet radiation from sunlight

explanation: Biological agents are living organisms like bacteria, viruses, or fungi that can cause infections. Great job keeping your categories straight!

question: What happens at the cellular level right before a seizure manifests physically?

options.A: The spinal cord blocks all sensory signals to the brain
options.B: Brain cells completely stop receiving oxygenated blood
options.C: Neurons permanently lose their ability to communicate
options.D: A large group of neurons fires abnormally and simultaneously

explanation: Seizures occur when synchronized, excessive electrical discharges sweep through a network of brain cells. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h2)

question: What type of information belongs in a standard incident report?

options.A: Derogatory remarks about an uncooperative patient
options.B: Personal opinions on which doctor or nurse caused the problem
options.C: Detailed theories on how much money the hospital might lose
options.D: Objective facts about what happened and actions taken

explanation: Correct! Incident reports need pure, unbiased facts—just the plain truth of what happened and what care was given right away.

question: A patient who had a laparoscopic tubal ligation two hours ago complains of sharp pain in her right shoulder. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Reassure her that trapped carbon dioxide gas causes this and encourage walking.
options.B: Administer a strong narcotic pain killer and restrict her to strict bed rest.
options.C: Notify the surgeon immediately because internal bleeding has reached her chest.
options.D: Apply an ice pack directly over her right shoulder joint to reduce inflammation.

explanation: Referred shoulder pain is very common after laparoscopy because residual abdominal gas irritates the diaphragm, and walking helps the body absorb it faster. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h5)

question: Which sign separates severe hyperemesis gravidarum from normal morning sickness?

options.A: Weight loss exceeding five percent of body weight
options.B: Mild fatigue during the afternoon hours
options.C: Queasiness that improves by the second trimester
options.D: Occasional dislike for the smell of coffee

explanation: Losing more than 5% of pre-pregnancy body weight tells us it's no longer regular morning sickness—it's hyperemesis and needs medical help!

question: Why do non-communicable diseases (NCDs) like hypertension often go unnoticed for years?

options.A: Symptoms only appear after a person reaches retirement age
options.B: They develop silently in the body without immediate noticeable symptoms
options.C: Standard diagnostic laboratory tests cannot detect chronic illnesses early
options.D: Patients refuse to visit primary health centres for routine check-ups

explanation: Spot on! Conditions like high blood pressure creep up slowly without causing obvious pain or distress. That's why routine checks are so important for your patients.

question: What is the main goal of community engagement in reproductive health?

options.A: Training foreign doctors to work in local clinics
options.B: Building more hospitals in rural communities
options.C: Reducing the cost of medical equipment importation
options.D: Involving local people directly in addressing health issues

explanation: Community engagement focuses on working side by side with local populations so they can actively shape health interventions that affect them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h1)

question: How do friendships usually shift as a teen moves from middle to late adolescence?

options.A: Social interactions stop happening outside of school
options.B: Friends become completely unimportant to the individual
options.C: Peer group pressure decreases as personal independence grows
options.D: Family influence disappears completely overnight

explanation: Correct! While friends are everything in middle adolescence, older teens get more comfortable standing on their own two feet and trusting their own choices.

question: A patient is very anxious about tests for a suspected adrenal tumor. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to refuse all invasive tests until they feel calmer
options.B: Provide clear, simple explanations of the tests and offer emotional support
options.C: Administer a strong sedative without a doctor's prescription
options.D: Reassure the patient that adrenal tumors are never cancerous

explanation: You're a natural! Clear, compassionate communication and emotional support go a long way in calming patient fears and helping them through tests.

question: Which of these is a common complication if an eye irrigation is done carelessly?

options.A: Corneal abrasion from equipment or trapped debris
options.B: Permanent systemic high blood pressure
options.C: Total loss of the patient's sense of smell
options.D: Sudden fracture of the orbital cheekbone

explanation: Rough handling or dragging particles across the eye can scratch the delicate cornea. Always be gentle!

question: Which scenario best demonstrates the function of sensory association areas?

options.A: Recognizing a hot cup of tea by its steam, warmth, and aroma together
options.B: Feeling a sharp pinprick on the skin and pulling the hand away quickly
options.C: Hearing a loud sudden sound and turning the head toward the noise
options.D: Blinking automatically when a bright light flashes in front of the eyes

explanation: Recognizing an object by combining multiple sensory cues like sight, temperature, and smell requires sensory association areas. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h7)

question: Which gender-related pressure often leads to higher rates of sexually transmitted infections among young males?

options.A: Strict adherence to solitary domestic lifestyles
options.B: Complete abstinence from all social gatherings
options.C: Fear of asking healthcare workers for vitamins
options.D: Pressure to prove masculinity through multiple partners

explanation: That's right! Societal pressure telling boys they must have multiple partners to 'prove' their manhood can unfortunately spread infections quickly.

question: A public health nurse writes a summary stating that teenage mothers in a rural ward have high rates of anemia due to poor nutrition and lack of antenatal care. What is this process called?

options.A: Hospital triage
options.B: Medical prescription
options.C: Community diagnosis
options.D: Surgical audit

explanation: Synthesizing data to identify health deficits, vulnerable groups, and causes in a population is known as a community diagnosis. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h4)

question: A nurse tells a doctor: 'The patient's blood pressure is dropping and urine output has stopped.' Which part of SBAR is this?

options.A: Background
options.B: Recommendation
options.C: Situation
options.D: Documentation

explanation: Describing what is happening right at this exact moment is the 'Situation' part of SBAR.

question: How did the role of the nurse change with the introduction of coronary care units?

options.A: Nurses were trained to independently spot dangerous rhythms and start emergency defibrillation
options.B: Nurses handed over all emergency response duties entirely to specialized physicians
options.C: Nurses focused solely on administering oral medications prescribed at shift change
options.D: Nurses were restricted from touching cardiac monitors without direct written doctor orders

explanation: Because cardiac arrest happens instantly, CCU nurses had to be trained to act immediately without waiting for a physician. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why are toddlers so prone to accidental poisoning at home?

options.A: Their natural curiosity drives them to taste and explore colorful items
options.B: Parents frequently leave dangerous medications inside school bags
options.C: Toddlers are usually employed to handle agricultural pesticides
options.D: They possess a high genetic tolerance for household chemicals

explanation: Exactly! Little ones love to explore everything using their mouths, often mistaking bright chemicals or syrups for sweet treats.

question: Why is severe fluid in the abdomen (ascites) a big risk during a liver biopsy?

options.A: It destroys all clotting factors in the blood
options.B: It makes the liver float around, making it hard to hit the target with the needle
options.C: It stops numbing medicine from working on the skin
options.D: It makes the patient stop breathing entirely

explanation: That's right! Too much fluid makes the liver shift position, meaning the needle might miss the spot or accidentally poke something else.

question: Which foetal blood shunt connects the pulmonary artery straight to the descending aorta?

options.A: Ductus venosus
options.B: Ductus arteriosus
options.C: Umbilical vein
options.D: Foramen ovale

explanation: Great job! The ductus arteriosus safely redirects blood away from the baby's unventilated lungs directly into the aorta. Foetal circulation is fascinating once you get the hang of it!

question: How do you calculate the mean (average) of a set of numbers?

options.A: Find the exact middle number after sorting values from lowest to highest
options.B: Add all values together and divide by the total number of values
options.C: Subtract the lowest number from the highest number in the group
options.D: Identify the single value that appears most frequently in the data set

explanation: The mean is simply your standard arithmetic average! Just add up all your observations and divide by how many there are.

question: Which serious infection can easily spread by sharing unsterilized blades during scarification?

options.A: Typhoid fever
options.B: Common malaria
options.C: Hepatitis B
options.D: Simple cholera

explanation: Exactly! Unclean cutting tools transfer blood-borne viruses like Hepatitis B and HIV directly from person to person. Safety first!

question: A patient scheduled for a spinal tap is currently taking warfarin for a heart condition. What is the nurse's best action?

options.A: Notify the doctor immediately about the bleeding risk
options.B: Proceed with the tap quickly before the next drug dose
options.C: Apply a hot pack to the lower back to thin the blood
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink extra water right away

explanation: Great job! Blood thinners increase the risk of bleeding into the spinal canal, so the doctor must be informed right away.

question: What crucial advice must a nurse give to a male patient who has just recovered from Ebola?

options.A: Return to the isolation ward immediately for another vaccine
options.B: Use barrier contraception or practice safe sex because the virus can linger in semen
options.C: Take daily antibiotics to clear the virus from your joints
options.D: Avoid all physical contact with family forever

explanation: Spot on! The virus can hide in certain body fluids long after recovery, so safe sex guidance is a must for male survivors.

question: Why must mast cell stabilizer sprays or drops be used regularly *before* an allergy season starts?

options.A: They interact with stomach acid if taken after an allergic attack starts.
options.B: They prevent cell rupture proactively but cannot reverse a reaction already underway.
options.C: They build up a thick physical barrier inside the nose that blocks dust.
options.D: They take at least two full weeks to enter the bloodstream for the first time.

explanation: Exactly! Think of them as prevention champs—they stop cells from popping, but they can't clean up the mess if the histamine has already spilled out.

question: Right after finishing a sterile dressing change, what final detail should you write on the dressing tape?

options.A: The hospital's insurance billing code.
options.B: The date, time, and your initials.
options.C: The patient's diagnosis and room number.
options.D: A friendly smiley face for the patient.

explanation: Labeling your work lets the rest of the healthcare team know exactly when the dressing was changed and who did it. Professional habit unlocked!

question: When does emergency contraception work most effectively?

options.A: When taken as soon as possible after unprotected sex
options.B: When administered right before the start of a menstrual period
options.C: When combined with daily prenatal vitamin supplements
options.D: When swallowed exactly fourteen days after ovulation

explanation: Time is everything! Emergency pills work best when taken promptly before ovulation happens.

question: How do tight budgets usually affect a clinical research study?

options.A: They automatically improve the accuracy of patient records
options.B: They limit sample sizes and shorten follow-up periods
options.C: They make patients more willing to take experimental drugs
options.D: They eliminate the need for ethical board review

explanation: Exactly! Without enough funding, researchers simply cannot afford to track as many people or follow them for very long.

question: If a patient has a pituitary problem that blocks LH and FSH, what is the most likely result?

options.A: Delayed or absent pubertal development
options.B: Excessive height and rapid bone growth
options.C: Severe reduction in daily urine output
options.D: Permanent high blood pressure

explanation: Correct! Without LH and FSH to prompt the sex organs, hormone production drops, which can delay or prevent normal puberty.

question: Why is setting specific check-in times helpful when caring for a patient with illness anxiety?

options.A: It forces the patient to stay confined to their bed all day
options.B: It guarantees that a physician will discover a hidden disease
options.C: It eliminates the need for any psychiatric medications
options.D: It reduces the constant, disruptive demands for continuous reassurance

explanation: Having a structured schedule shows the patient they are supported without letting endless health fixation take over the whole shift.

question: Which surgical method uses metal plates, screws, or rods attached directly to the bone?

options.A: Endoscopic joint debridement
options.B: Closed manual skin traction
options.C: External pin frame fixation
options.D: Open reduction internal fixation

explanation: ORIF involves a surgical incision to place hardware directly on or inside the bone to hold pieces firmly in place. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h7)

question: What is a major health risk when growing infants are denied protein-rich foods because of cultural myths?

options.A: Faster physical growth
options.B: Improved natural immunity
options.C: Stronger bone density
options.D: Malnutrition and stunting

explanation: Withholding essential building blocks like protein from growing children frequently leads to malnutrition and delayed physical growth. Good nutrition education changes lives here!

question: Chronic kidney disease is diagnosed in a pregnant woman if kidney trouble or protein in the urine is found before which gestational week?

options.A: Before fourteen weeks
options.B: Before ten weeks
options.C: Before thirty weeks
options.D: Before twenty weeks

explanation: Great to know! If signs show up before the twentieth week, it usually means the kidney issue was already there before the pregnancy started.

question: What is the single best way to stop germs from spreading during patient care?

options.A: Avoiding all physical contact with patients
options.B: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.C: Wearing sterile gowns at all times
options.D: Using scented room sprays

explanation: Simple handwashing or using hand sanitiser is your superpower against infections. It washes away those sneaky microbes before they can jump to the next patient!

question: Which of these is a common reason a patient would need a laryngoscopy?

options.A: Severe abdominal pain
options.B: Persistent hoarseness
options.C: Lower leg swelling
options.D: High blood pressure

explanation: Well done! If someone's voice has been unusually rough or hoarse for a long time, doctors use a laryngoscopy to take a closer look at the vocal cords.

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse needs to teach a patient recovering from a hysteroscopic polyp removal?

options.A: Reporting fever or worsening pelvic pain
options.B: Understanding when sexual activity can safely resume
options.C: How to perform daily abdominal wound dressing changes
options.D: Recognizing signs of heavy vaginal bleeding

explanation: Correct! Because hysteroscopy is done entirely through the natural passages (vagina and cervix), there are no abdominal cuts or dressings to worry about.

question: What is the very first step of urine formation in the kidney?

options.A: Tubular secretion
options.B: Glomerular filtration
options.C: Peristaltic propulsion
options.D: Tubular reabsorption

explanation: Everything starts at the glomerulus! Blood pressure forces water and small particles out of the blood and into Bowman's capsule to kick off urine making.

question: A young man is rushed to the emergency ward after sniffing petrol from a container. What immediate danger should you watch out for?

options.A: Chronic kidney stone formation and severe bone pain
options.B: Sudden permanent blindness from optic nerve damage
options.C: Immediate high blood pressure and rapid weight gain
options.D: Respiratory depression and central nervous system toxicity

explanation: Inhalants like petrol quickly slow down the brain, which can dangerously stop a person from breathing properly. Always monitor the airway first!

question: How many abdominal quadrants do clinicians use for a quick physical assessment?

options.A: Nine
options.B: Six
options.C: Four
options.D: Two

explanation: The abdomen is divided into four quadrants using vertical and horizontal lines crossing at the belly button. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T2#GNS111_U1_T2_h6)

question: A child keeps coming back to the clinic with severe diarrhea. What should you check first?

options.A: Assessing the family's source of drinking water and home sanitation
options.B: Telling the mother to stop feeding the child local home-cooked meals
options.C: Prescribing stronger antibiotics and keeping the child in the ward
options.D: Advising the parents to move to a different country entirely

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! Repeated diarrhea usually points to dirty water or poor home hygiene, so checking the root cause stops the cycle.

question: Why should nurses actively involve family caregivers in disease management education?

options.A: It removes all responsibility from the professional nurse.
options.B: It helps caregivers spot red flags and offer safe daily support.
options.C: It prevents the patient from ever speaking to a doctor.
options.D: It ensures the family takes over financial medical costs.

explanation: Family members are with the patient every day. Training them means someone is always watching for warning signs when you aren't there.

question: What is the main reason traditional healers make therapeutic cuts on the body?

options.A: To rub local herbal medicine into the body
options.B: To permanently change the person's facial shape
options.C: To remove unwanted body hair follicles
options.D: To test the pain tolerance of young children

explanation: That's right! These cuts help local remedies absorb directly into the skin or tissues for quicker healing according to traditional beliefs.

question: What is the single biggest reason adolescents stay away from health clinics?

options.A: Having to wear a hospital gown
options.B: Fear of breach of privacy and confidentiality
options.C: Lack of parking spaces outside the hospital
options.D: The bright lighting inside the examination room

explanation: Correct! Teens worry that nurses or doctors might gossip or share their private health details with family members.

question: Which symptom is a major warning sign for bladder cancer?

options.A: Painless gross hematuria
options.B: Painful swelling of the knee joints
options.C: Complete inability to sweat
options.D: Severe sudden right-side flank pain

explanation: Gross hematuria means blood in the urine that you can actually see with the naked eye. When it comes on without any pain, it's a classic red flag for the bladder.

question: What is the primary condition treated using emergency inhaled bronchodilators?

options.A: Acute bronchospasm
options.B: Lower extremity deep vein thrombosis
options.C: Chronic bacterial skin infection
options.D: Severe iron-deficiency anemia

explanation: Bronchodilators relax tightened airway muscles, making them the primary treatment for sudden breathing constriction or asthma attacks. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which type of estrogen is the strongest and most active during a woman's reproductive years?

options.A: Estriol
options.B: Estradiol
options.C: Estrone
options.D: Eplerenone

explanation: Estradiol is the heavy hitter! It's produced in the highest amounts by the ovaries and drives most estrogen activity before menopause.

question: What makes the copper IUD special compared to emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: It is only effective if taken within the first two hours
options.B: It must be swallowed as a tablet with a full glass of water
options.C: It provides ongoing long-term birth control after emergency use
options.D: It permanently stops a woman from ever having children

explanation: The copper IUD is a double-whammy: it works as emergency contraception right now, and it can stay in place to prevent pregnancy for years. Super convenient!

question: You are preparing a suction catheter for an adult patient with an artificial airway. What is the rule of thumb for selecting the catheter size?

options.A: It must be the largest possible size that fits through the opening
options.B: It should always be a uniform size 14 French regardless of the tube
options.C: It should fill the entire inside of the tube to grab all the mucus
options.D: It should take up no more than half the inner diameter of the airway

explanation: Leaving enough open space around the catheter prevents a vacuum from forming inside the lungs, which would dangerously drop oxygen levels. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h3)

question: A grieving family member moves rapidly between intense anger at hospital staff and deep depression within the same hour. What does this behavior indicate?

options.A: Normal fluctuation through non-linear grief stages
options.B: A pathological personality disorder requiring isolation
options.C: A failure of the nursing staff to communicate clearly
options.D: An intentional attempt to manipulate caregivers

explanation: Grief is fluid, and individuals frequently move back and forth between different stages rather than following a straight line. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which detail is NOT required when documenting a new peripheral IV insertion?

options.A: The catheter gauge and anatomical location
options.B: The brand name of the soap used for handwashing
options.C: The patient's response and tolerance to the procedure
options.D: The date and exact time of the insertion

explanation: Standard hand hygiene is assumed; charting focuses on the specific procedure details like size, location, time, and patient response. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h10)

question: What common foot problem does a footboard primarily prevent in patients who are on bed rest?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Pressure ulcers on the heels
options.C: Hypostatic pneumonia
options.D: Foot drop

explanation: Brilliant! A footboard holds the feet in a natural upright position, stopping the Achilles tendon from tightening up and causing permanent foot drop.

question: What is the main role of apoptosis in the body?

options.A: Removing damaged or unneeded cells in a neat, orderly way
options.B: Causing sudden inflammation after an injury
options.C: Turning normal tissue into tumors
options.D: Encouraging rapid stem cell division

explanation: Correct! Apoptosis is the body's clean-up process—it gently removes old or damaged cells without causing messy inflammation.

question: Which medication is absolutely essential for a patient living with Type 1 diabetes to survive?

options.A: Metformin
options.B: Acarbose
options.C: Sulfonylurea
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Because Type 1 bodies cannot make insulin, daily insulin replacement is a matter of survival. Another win for your clinical knowledge today!

question: What happens to the bladder and urethra during 'urethral hypermobility' when a patient coughs?

options.A: The bladder instantly shrinks in size
options.B: The urethral sphincter locks tightly shut to block flow
options.C: The detrusor muscle contracts with too much force
options.D: The bladder and urethra drop downward due to weak support

explanation: When the pelvic tissues are a bit weak, coughing causes the bladder and urethra to sag downward instead of staying firmly in place.

question: How do diuretic medications generally help the body get rid of extra water?

options.A: By destroying waste products in the renal cortex
options.B: By increasing blood flow directly to the glomerulus
options.C: By stopping the production of water in the liver
options.D: By blocking sodium reabsorption in the nephron

explanation: Think of diuretics as helpers that stop the nephron from reabsorbing sodium. Water naturally follows sodium, so both stay in the urine and leave the body!

question: What happens if just one link breaks in the vaccine cold chain?

options.A: The vaccine automatically adjusts its own temperature
options.B: The vaccine potency can be permanently lost
options.C: The packaging becomes sterile automatically
options.D: The expiration date of the product extends

explanation: Vaccines are very delicate biological products. If they get too warm or too cold, they lose their power to protect—even if they look completely normal!

question: What main event tells you the third stage of labour is happening?

options.A: The stabilization of maternal vital signs postpartum
options.B: Full dilation of the maternal cervix
options.C: Expulsion of the placenta and fetal membranes
options.D: The physical birth of the newborn baby

explanation: The baby is already born in stage three, so this stage is all about safely delivering the placenta.

question: Why must you always ask patients about any herbal remedies they take alongside prescription drugs?

options.A: Some herbs can dangerously alter the effects of prescribed medications
options.B: Traditional plants always neutralize standard hospital equipment
options.C: Herbal remedies are illegal to consume in any home care setting
options.D: Doctors refuse to document any natural products in the chart

explanation: Spot on! Herbs are active substances. Mixing them with hospital drugs can accidentally boost or block the medication, causing dangerous side effects.

question: Which routine nursing task calls for clean examination gloves?

options.A: Measuring a patient's resting blood pressure
options.B: Handing a clean meal tray to a patient
options.C: Adjusting nasal cannula oxygen flow
options.D: Emptying a urinary catheter drainage bag

explanation: Urine is a body fluid, so you definitely want glove protection to avoid exposure when emptying that drainage bag. Simple and safe!

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to ensure a health project is sustainable?

options.A: Involving village leaders in planning from the very beginning
options.B: Relying entirely on foreign staff to make every daily decision
options.C: Using affordable materials available within the local market
options.D: Training local residents as community health volunteers

explanation: Depending completely on outside staff creates dependency and guarantees the project will fail once those outsiders leave. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: A patient is given a drug that blocks acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction. What happens as a result?

options.A: Muscle relaxation and paralysis
options.B: Increased action potential speed
options.C: Rapid muscle hypertrophy
options.D: Uncontrolled muscle spasms

explanation: If the chemical messenger can't deliver its message because the receptors are blocked, the muscle simply cannot receive the signal to contract. That leads to relaxation and paralysis! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h3)

question: How does the common pill warfarin work in the body?

options.A: By stopping the bone marrow from producing platelets
options.B: By dissolving fibrin threads in established blood clots
options.C: By directly neutralizing circulating thrombin molecules
options.D: By blocking the liver from using Vitamin K to make clotting factors

explanation: Warfarin teams up against Vitamin K! By blocking it in the liver, the body temporarily slows down its production of key clotting proteins.

question: Why do health organizations strongly oppose 'medicalization'—which is performing FGM in a clinic by trained health workers?

options.A: It always causes immediate death from surgical shock
options.B: It increases the cost of healthcare services for the government
options.C: It prevents doctors from treating other common diseases
options.D: It validates and perpetuates a human rights violation rather than stopping it

explanation: Well reasoned! Doing FGM in a clinic gives a harmful practice fake medical approval instead of tackling the root gender inequality and abuse.

question: In which clinical situation would a doctor most likely use an intraarterial route?

options.A: Administering a routine morning dose of oral antibiotics
options.B: Providing daily maintenance fluids for a stable surgical patient
options.C: Giving an intramuscular vaccination for tetanus prevention
options.D: Delivering targeted chemotherapy directly to a liver tumor

explanation: Spot on! When doctors want to hit a specific trouble spot—like a tumor—with maximum medicine power without flooding the whole body, the intraarterial route is super useful.

question: What is the minimum legal age of marriage stipulated by the Nigerian Child Rights Act?

options.A: 15 years
options.B: 21 years
options.C: 18 years
options.D: 16 years

explanation: The Child Rights Act designates any individual under 18 years as a child and prohibits their marriage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h4)

question: Which chemical messengers in the brain play a major role in mood and depression?

options.A: Serotonin and norepinephrine
options.B: Insulin and glucagon
options.C: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.D: Sodium and potassium

explanation: Well done! Serotonin and norepinephrine are key neurotransmitters that help regulate our mood. An imbalance here is a big part of why depression happens.

question: What are the two main cavities that divide the inside of the human body?

options.A: dorsal and ventral body cavities
options.B: thoracic and abdominopelvic cavities
options.C: serous and mucous membrane layers
options.D: cranial and spinal body regions

explanation: You've got this! The human body splits its main internal spaces into the dorsal cavity at the back and the ventral cavity at the front.

question: Where is the safest place to give a vitamin K injection to a full-term newborn?

options.A: Ventral gluteal muscle
options.B: Vastus lateralis muscle
options.C: Deltoid muscle of the arm
options.D: Dorsogluteal muscle

explanation: The vastus lateralis in the outer thigh is the go-to spot! It's well-developed in newborns and keeps them safe from major nerves and blood vessels.

question: A patient is given a strong opioid pain medication. Which assessment is most important for the nurse to perform shortly after?

options.A: Respiratory rate and depth
options.B: Bowel sound frequency in all quadrants
options.C: Visual acuity and reading ability
options.D: Skin color on the palms of the hands

explanation: Opioids depress the central nervous system, making respiratory depression a dangerous complication that requires close monitoring. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which of these clinical actions goes against the rules of rational drug use?

options.A: Prescribing strong broad-spectrum antibiotics for a simple viral upper respiratory infection
options.B: Educating a diabetic patient on the correct technique for self-administering insulin
options.C: Administering a standard dose of paracetamol for a documented fever in an adult
options.D: Checking a patient's kidney function before starting a new maintenance medication

explanation: Remember: antibiotics fight bacteria, not viruses! Giving them for a simple cold or viral infection wastes medicine and causes drug resistance.

question: An older adult patient admitted with dizziness tries to get out of bed unassisted to use the bathroom. What is the best immediate preventive action?

options.A: Tie the patient's hands securely to the bed railings
options.B: Turn off the room lights so the patient stays in bed to sleep
options.C: Scold the patient for trying to walk without asking first
options.D: Respond quickly to the call bell and assist the patient to walk

explanation: Answering call lights promptly and providing physical support during movement keeps unsteady patients safe without resorting to unsafe restraints. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h4)

question: How do social and environmental factors affect a person's emotional state?

options.A: They completely override all biological influences in the human brain
options.B: They have zero effect once a person reaches adulthood
options.C: Economic stability and community support systems directly shape resilience and stress levels
options.D: They only matter if the person has a diagnosed physical disease

explanation: Our surroundings matter! Things like financial stress, safety, and having a good support system directly impact how much daily stress we carry.

question: A nurse sets up a free blood pressure check at the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Primordial prevention

explanation: You nailed it! Secondary prevention is about catching health issues early through screening before they cause major trouble.

question: What is the biggest challenge faced by child-headed households?

options.A: The government evicts them immediately for breaking zoning laws
options.B: Children lack adult guidance, financial stability, and legal protection
options.C: They are required by law to run community health clinics
options.D: They receive too much financial support from international donors

explanation: When young ones live alone without an adult, everyday survival becomes a massive struggle for food, shelter, and safety. Community nurses play a key role in identifying and helping them.

question: Which test directly confirms a diagnosis of polycythaemia vera?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: JAK2 gene mutation assay
options.C: Coagulation profile test
options.D: Serum iron and ferritin panel

explanation: Running a JAK2 gene test is the go-to way to confirm primary polycythaemia vera at the cellular level.

question: A teenager expresses a belief that getting pregnant or catching an infection is impossible for them. Which psychological concept is this youth displaying?

options.A: Cognitive dissonance
options.B: Depressive withdrawal
options.C: Prefrontal cortex maturity
options.D: Personal invulnerability

explanation: Believing that negative health outcomes only affect other people is a classic sign of the adolescent sense of personal invulnerability. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h3)

question: What legal idea lets a patient sue a hospital for a contractor's mistake because the hospital made it look like the worker was their staff?

options.A: Apparent agency
options.B: Respondeat superior
options.C: Stare decisis
options.D: Habeas corpus

explanation: 'Apparent agency' happens when the hospital's setup leads a patient to reasonably believe a contractor is a regular staff member.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common consequence of relying solely on a free market for healthcare?

options.A: Universal and equal access for all citizens regardless of wealth
options.B: Neglect of unprofitable public health services
options.C: Lack of basic care for uninsured populations
options.D: Geographic concentration of hospitals in wealthy urban areas

explanation: A pure free market distributes care based on ability to pay, which naturally creates disparities rather than universal equal access. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h5)

question: How does a public health nurse's daily role differ from a nurse working on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Agency nurses never interact with actual human patients
options.B: Agency nurses focus on community-wide prevention rather than individual bedside treatment
options.C: Hospital nurses write all national healthcare laws
options.D: Agency nurses only dispense emergency medications

explanation: Well done! Ward nurses care for patients one-on-one at the bedside, while public health nurses look at whole communities and prevention strategies.

question: What is the main purpose of a variance report in nursing management?

options.A: To calculate individual nurse salaries and performance bonuses
options.B: To assess patient physical recovery rates after surgery
options.C: To determine which medical equipment manufacturers to sue
options.D: To compare budgeted financial targets with actual expenses

explanation: Variance reports show where financial goals were hit or missed, helping managers make smart adjustments for the future.

question: You are packing vaccines to take to a remote village for a community outreach day. What should you use to carry them?

options.A: Vaccine carrier with conditioned ice packs
options.B: An open plastic bucket with regular ice cubes
options.C: A large walk-in freezer unit
options.D: A cardboard box lined with newspapers

explanation: Vaccine carriers are portable and insulated, making them perfect for keeping your outreach supplies safe for a day out in the field.
